work_identified: Claudii Galeni Opera Omnia Vol. 18 Pt. 2 (Kühn ed., Leipzig 1830): a Greek-Latin bilingual volume containing Galen's commentaries on Hippocratic surgical texts — confirmed to include In Hippocratis librum De Fracturis commentarii (ending at p.628) and In Hippocratis librum De Officina Medici commentarii III (starting p.629); Vol. 18A/18B numbering places this as the second half of Kühn vol. 18, after the Aphorisms commentary ends at XVIIIA 195

reasoning: Vol. 18 Pt. 2 (Kühn 1830, ~1030pp) contains Galen's commentary on Hippocrates' De Fracturis (ending p.628) and De Officina Medici (p.629+); possibly also parts of the De Articulis commentary. None of these surgical Hippocratic commentaries has a complete published English translation. Scholar W.J. Lewis (ancientmedicine.org, 2021) explicitly states 'it's almost impossible to find English translations of Galen's Hippocratic commentaries.' The Cambridge Galen Translations series — the leading scholarly English-translation project — has not published any of these texts. Only prefaces have appeared online (not scholarly complete translations). Absence confirmed in tradition-appropriate sources: Cambridge series, Online Books (UPenn), Wellcome, BMCR.
